question.text: Under Rule 9(16) of the PML Rules, when Aadhaar authentication is not required for establishing a client's identity, what is the obligation in respect of the Aadhaar number on the document submitted?

answer.text: The reporting entity/intermediary must ensure that the client redacts or blacks out the Aadhaar number
The reporting entity has no responsibility; the client may or may not redact the Aadhaar number
The Central KYC Records Registry (CKYCR) must redact the Aadhaar number during processing
No redaction is needed as the Aadhaar number is always required for KYC

explanation.text: The Logic: The PML Rules and the related SEBI provisions require that where Aadhaar authentication is not required, the reporting entity/intermediary shall ensure that the client redacts or blacks out the Aadhaar number while submitting a copy of the Aadhaar card. The Trap: Although the physical act of redaction is performed by the client, the duty to ensure that the redaction happens is placed on the reporting entity/intermediary. Saying the reporting entity has no responsibility is therefore incorrect. Note: Aadhaar is not always mandatory for identity verification — clients may use other OVDs — so blanket statements that no redaction is ever needed are also incorrect.
